1,200 repositories. 🤯

When we launched Patchwork CI, we made a promise: always free for open source. Many people told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Fast forward to today — we're running on 1,200 repositories, and about 900 of them are open source. 💚

But here's what truly blew my mind 👇

Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test.

Let that sink in. 1 in 7.

That's countless hours of developer time wasted on red builds that weren't real failures.

Open source didn't just give us users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. In fact, our most-requested feature — GitLab support — came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12. 🚀

Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic
pairs.a:
Patchwork CI is on 1,200 repositories now. About 900 of them are open source, where it's free.

The free tier gave us something I didn't expect: data. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test, not a real bug.

The open-source maintainers also told us what to build next. GitLab support was their most-requested feature. We shipped it on November 12.

If you're deciding whether a free tier is worth it for a dev tool: for us, it paid off in data and direction before it paid in money.
pairs.b: Patchwork CI promised to be free for open source.  Many people told us we were crazy. “How will you make money?” they asked.  Fast forward to today: we’re running on 1,200 repositories.  About 900 of them are open source.  That’s a lot of good things.  Here’s what truly blew my mind:  Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test.  Let that sink in.  1 in 7.  That’s countless hours of developer time wasted on red builds that weren’t real failures.  Open source didn’t just give us users.  It gave us data, feedback, and a community.  In fact, our most-requested feature — GitLab support — came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.  Giving back isn’t charity.  It’s strategy.

pairs.draft:
Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline. 💡

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

But here's the thing — failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason? They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what great teams do: we listened. We learned. We built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. Not just a feature — a fundamental shift in how we think about our customers.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson? Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough. 🚀

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build — you just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company? 👇

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth
pairs.a:
Our first big customer left Ledgerline after 5 months.

They had customised NetSuite heavily, and we only handled the standard fields. For a setup like theirs, we simply didn't fit.

We spent the next 6 weeks adding support for custom fields.

We have 38 customers now. 11 of them use custom fields.

What I took from it: when a customer leaves, ask which part of their real setup you didn't handle. It's usually something specific, and you can usually build it.

3 days. That's how long one spindle failure shut down our line. ⏰

Years ago, I was a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune. One day, a spindle failed — and an entire production line ground to a halt for 3 long days. 😓

But here's the part that still haunts me:

The warning signs were there. 2 weeks earlier, vibration readings had clearly shown the problem.

No one was watching. 👀

That moment changed everything for me. In 2022, I founded Ferrous with one mission: to make sure no manufacturer ever has to experience that kind of preventable downtime again.

Today, our sensors are on 410 machines across 17 plants. 🏭

Every reading is a story. Every alert is a breakdown avoided. Every plant is a step closer to the future of Indian manufacturing. 🇮🇳

Data is only powerful if someone is listening. 💡

#Manufacturing #Industry40 #PredictiveMaintenance #MakeInIndia #StartupStory
pairs.a:
I was a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune when a spindle failed and stopped a line for 3 days.

The vibration readings had shown the problem 2 weeks earlier. Nobody was watching them.

That's why I started Ferrous in 2022: so someone is watching.

Our sensors are on 410 machines across 17 plants now.

If you run a plant, ask who would notice if a vibration reading changed this week. If the answer is "nobody in particular," that's the gap.
